text:
Nick Suzuki won the Selke last season while scoring 101 points, and Evolving-Hockey had him fourth of 401 forwards in wins above replacement. He missed time early this fall, and since coming back with a three-point game he's been the same player: 16 points in 12 games, with the Canadiens taking 59% of the expected goals at five on five when he's on.

There's some luck in the start. Montreal has scored 5.2 more goals than expected with him on the ice, padding his points, and his rate (3.8 points per 60) sits at the very top of our range. Evolving-Hockey also noted his 2025-26 results ran a little ahead of his chances.

But the two-way game is the point. He takes chances away (86th percentile last season) and still sets up teammates at a high rate in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking. Connor McDavid and Mitch Marner have had glowing things to say about him lately. Our range: 79 to 110 points.
